entry.title: antcc Fixes -O2 Performance Pessimization in Lua Benchmarks
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | 386s.org | discussion

The developer of the antcc C compiler identified a performance regression where -O2 builds were significantly slower than -O1 builds when benchmarking Lua. The issue was traced to excessive register pressure during register allocation, where over 40% of instructions in the Lua interpreter loop were stack-to-register move operations. This was caused by the mem2reg pass incorrectly generating loop-carried phi instructions for variables that were actually local to specific control flow branches, leading to an unintended expansion of the binary size.

The root cause was an issue in the SSA construction algorithm's handling of uninitialized variables. The mem2reg pass allowed recursive lookups to traverse loop back-edges, causing the compiler to incorrectly treat variables as being live across entire loop iterations. A fix was implemented to explicitly initialize variables as undefined at the alloca stage, which prevents the insertion of these erroneous phi functions and eliminates the performance penalty.

In a modular proof system, a trait implementation must establish that all supertrait requirements are met. entry.content:
Lobsters Top | sebsite.pw | discussion

C string-to-float conversion functions like `strtod`, `strtof`, and `strtold` present challenges for portable error detection due to conflicting requirements between the C standard and POSIX. While the C standard uses the `math_errhandling` macro to determine whether to signal errors via `errno` or floating-point exceptions, POSIX mandates that `errno` be set for both overflow and underflow scenarios. This discrepancy leads to inconsistent behavior across different C libraries, such as glibc and musl, where one might set `errno` on invalid input while another does not.

To ensure robust error handling, developers must use the `endptr` parameter to verify if a conversion was successful. For overflow and underflow, error detection requires implementation-specific strategies, such as checking `errno` for `ERANGE`, testing floating-point exception status, or performing manual string analysis, depending on whether the target environment follows POSIX or strict C standards.
